text: Knowledge gains meaning when it is grounded.
From lecture halls and laboratories to the public sphere,
the women professors of Nahdlatul Ulama now walk together—
for faith, for homeland, and for the nation.
This is the Association of Muslimat NU Professors — APMNU.
An intellectual and professional home for women professors
from the Nahdlatul Ulama community.
They span religion, social sciences, law, economics,
health, science and technology.
As part of the Muslimat NU family,
APMNU dedicates its expertise to faith, homeland, and nation,
within the framework of Ahlussunnah wal Jama'ah an-Nahdliyah.
The idea for APMNU was born at the Muslimat NU National Working Meeting in Samarinda,
when Khofifah Indar Parawansa saw the great potential of Muslimat NU's women professors.
The idea quickly took shape.
In February 2026, APMNU held its National Coordination Meeting in Surabaya,
discussing its statutes and bylaws.
Its board was inaugurated by the Chair of Muslimat NU's Advisory Board,
witnessed by the Minister of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
APMNU stands as a home for scholarship
rooted in Ahlussunnah wal Jamaah values.
Its direction is clear: education, research,
policy advocacy, and community empowerment,
backed by national and international networks.
Going forward, productive waqf will sustain the institution,
so ideas don't stay in the ivory tower but grow into real public good.
APMNU is led by Prof. Dr. Amany Lubis of UIN Syarif Hidayatullah Jakarta,
the first woman to serve as its rector.
With over sixty active board members and representatives in nearly every province,
APMNU works under the guidance of Khofifah Indar Parawansa,
Chair of Muslimat NU's Advisory Board.
Before the Congress, APMNU held a series of national webinars.
The first webinar, 'R.A. Kartini's Legacy for the Nation's Civilization,'
was held online on 21 April 2026,
presented by Prof. Dr. Phil. Sahiron Syamsuddin, Director of Diktis at Indonesia's Ministry of Religious Affairs.
On 2 May 2026, the webinar 'Inclusive and Child-Friendly Education'
was presented by Prof. Dr. Abdul Mu'ti,
Indonesia's Minister of Primary and Secondary Education.
Then on 20 May 2026, the webinar 'The Rise of Women Researchers in Indonesia'
was attended by Prof. Arif Satria,
Head of Indonesia's National Research and Innovation Agency (BRIN).
August 2026: the 35th Nahdlatul Ulama Congress in Jombang
became a key stage for APMNU.
At SMK Negeri 1 Jombang, APMNU held a National Seminar and Bahtsul Masail
on 'Building a Digitally Smart Generation and Environments Free from Sexual Violence.'
Eighty-two professors attended, from Sumatra, Kalimantan,
Sulawesi, Java and West Nusa Tenggara.
They discussed positive parenting, wise use of AI,
and preventing violence in schools.
At the same moment, APMNU launched three works:
the book 'Muslimat NU Responds to a Changing Era,'
APMNU's official website, and the Journal of Muslimat and Society.
APMNU's work also crosses borders.
Through an Academic Benchmarking Program in October 2026,
a delegation travelled to Egypt.
In Cairo, they visited the Indonesian Embassy
to strengthen Indonesia–Egypt academic ties.
They also attended the inauguration of Muslimat NU's
Special Branch in Egypt at Al-Azhar.
They also visited the Islamic Universities League in Cairo,
exploring collaboration with the global network of Islamic universities.
In Ismailia, the delegation was received by the President of Suez Canal University
to explore academic cooperation.
This network keeps growing.
Nearly two hundred professors are now listed in APMNU's directory,
across eighty-two study programs.
Together with Muslimat NU, they set two Indonesian MURI records:
the women's organization with the most women professors,
and the national forum with the most women professors across disciplines.
APMNU: for a Muslimat NU that is knowledgeable, empowered, and of service
to the community, the nation, and civilization.
For women professors of the Nahdliyin community, the door to service is open.
